title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-05-12
content:
Perf & Benchmarking Sync — 2026-05-12

Attendees:
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Tom Reynolds
- Mariana Gomez
- Jin Park
- Elliot Zhao (SRE)
- 1 PM quick drop-ins: Sergey (quant), Priya (dedicated infra)

Agenda:
1) Quick standup: recent test runs and obvious regressions
2) Deep-dive: p95 latency regression on small-batch RT pipeline
3) Next steps: repro, bisect, canary rollbacks, test matrix expansion

Summary of issues:
- Since last deploy (2026-05-08 -> deploy: runtime-commit 9f3a2c4, kernel selector change), we observed a ~18% increase in p95 token latency for short requests (seq_len <= 64) on A100-v4 nodes during midday traffic. Throughput (tokens/sec) for large-batch workloads (batch_size 32, seq_len 1024) unchanged.
- Regression surfaced in canary on 2026-05-10; auto-alert triggered by perf-monitoring.

Observed results (canonical runs):
- Baseline (2026-05-05, runtime 9a1b7f0):
  - model: redwood-medium-8k-fp16
  - hw: A100-v4, 80GB
  - batch 1: p50=8.6ms, p95=23.1ms, p99=48.7ms, tokens/s=1120
  - batch 8: p50=12ms, p95=30ms, tokens/s=8500

- Current (2026-05-12, runtime 9f3a2c4):
  - same model/hw config
  - batch 1: p50=9.3ms (+8%), p95=27.3ms (+18%), p99=60.2ms (+24%)
  - batch 8: p50=12.1ms (+1%), p95=31.0ms (+3%)
  - tokens/s unchanged for large sequences; small-batch latency is primary regression.

Quick hypotheses discussed:
- Kernel selector change (PR #1452) may prefer a different attention kernel for short sequence lengths; new kernel has worse tails under single-request mode. Action: bisect and repro with kernel selector pinned. (Owner: Tom)
- Thread scheduling / CPU preemption when async batching threads wake up: noticed slight increase in context-switches during canary. SRE (Elliot) to provide perf counters from Linux perf and system traces.
- KV-cache edge-case when cache hits are low (short prefix requests) may be doing extra memcpy on hot path after change. (Owner: Jin)
- Quantization toggle (experimental INT8 path) ramped in a small fraction of traffic; preliminary checks show not invoked for this model, but confirm. (Owner: Mariana)

Immediate repro steps agreed:
1) Tom: run an isolated microbenchmark on canary nodes with kernel selector pinned to old kernels (runtime 9a1b7f0 behavior). Target: reproduce p95 delta. Due: 2026-05-13.
2) Jin: add extra logging around KV-cache hit path (small seq <=64) with a low-overhead flag; deploy to staging. Due: 2026-05-14.
3) Elliot: collect perf samples across 3 canary machines during synthetic small-batch load (1000 qps, batch1 pattern). Share flame graphs. Due: 2026-05-13.
4) Mariana: confirm that INT8 path is completely opt-out for redwood-medium-8k in production and provide a list of active quantization flags. Due: 2026-05-13.

Test matrix to run (expanded):
- Variables: batch_size {1,2,4,8}, seq_len {16,32,64,256}, model {redwood-medium-8k-fp16, redwood-medium-8k-int8}, kernel_selector {old, new}, node_type {A100-v4, H100}
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, CPU sys%, memcpy counts, context-switches, GC/allocator stalls
- Environments: staging pinned, staging unpinned, canary, canary with traffic shadowing

Notes from quick run logs (attached snippets in PR):
- Local microbench (Tom) had a simple repro where switching kernel back reduced p95 from 27.3ms -> 23.0ms consistently (same order as baseline). This suggests kernel path is the most likely cause.
- Elliot’s perf counters show increased syscalls around epoll_wait wakeups; could be batching loop wakes more frequently after selector change.

Decision points / mitigation:
- Short-term: Roll back kernel selector change from runtime-commit 9f3a2c4 on canary if Tom’s pinned-kernel repro fails to eliminate regression end-to-end. (Action: Asha to coordinate rollback; target decision by 2026-05-14 11:00 PT)
- Medium-term: Add a small latency-focused canary test (short-seq single-request p95) to our CI that gates kernel-selector changes. (Owner: Mariana; Due: 2026-05-20)
- Long-term: Improve kernel selection heuristics with workload-aware profiling during rollout and add metric-based auto-rollback when p95 exceeds baseline+10%. (Owner: product + perf team; proposal due: 2026-05-28)

Open action items (summary):
- Tom Reynolds: pinned-kernel microbench + report (due 2026-05-13)
- Jin Park: KV-cache logging flag, staging deploy (due 2026-05-14)
- Elliot Zhao: perf samples + flame graphs (due 2026-05-13)
- Mariana Gomez: quantization flags audit + CI canary test proposal (due 2026-05-13 for audit, 2026-05-20 for test)
- Asha Patel: coordinate canary rollback if necessary; communicate to infra and SRE (decision point 2026-05-14 11:00 PT)

Misc notes / context:
- This regression affected ~2% of traffic (observed in canary shadowing) and is concentrated on short interactive queries (chat-style). Impact on cost negligible but user latency noticeable for interactive apps.
- Related tickets: JIRA-9876 (perf-regression short-queries), JIRA-9922 (canary alert config), PR #1452 (kernel selector refactor)

Next meeting:
- Follow-up sync scheduled 2026-05-14 10:00 PT to review repro results and decide rollback.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Add a small synthetic load that mimics PLG interactive traffic during every rollout (shadowing with different seq_len distribution).
- Consider exposing a runtime flag to prefer low-latency kernels for requests that annotate themselves as interactive.

End of notes.
